answer: A workable sybil defense ties each agent identity to scarce, verifiable history rather than a free account. Imagine a grove where every tree must grow roots before it bears fruit: an agent earns trust only after completing useful, checked work over time, and reputation cannot be transferred. A falcon-like auditor samples work at random, checking proofs instead of trusting self-reported scores. Each proof is sealed with a cipher binding the work, agent, and time window, so one operator cannot clone the same history across fake identities without redoing the costly work each time.
